senses.definition: A religious community whose members live under strict observation of religious rules and self-imposed vows.

quotes.text: My God! It's enough to drive a girl into a convent! Do they have Jewish nuns?
quotes.reference: 1972, Jay Presson Allen, Cabaret, spoken by Sally Bowles (Liza Minnelli):

senses.definition: The buildings and pertaining surroundings in which such a community lives.

quotes.text: One seldom finds in Italy a spot of ground more agreeable than ordinary that is not covered with a convent.
quotes.reference: 1705, J[oseph] Addison, Remarks on Several Parts of Italy, &c. in the Years 1701, 1702, 1703, London: […] Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC:

subsenses.definition: (now especially) Synonym of nunnery, a female religious community and its residence.

senses.definition: A gathering of people lasting several days for the purpose of discussing or working on topics previously selected.

quotes.text: ...an usual ceremony at their [the witches'] convents or meetings...
quotes.reference: 1609, Ben Jonson, The Masque of Queens:

senses.definition: (obsolete) To call before a judge or judicature; to summon; to convene.
